__comment: Polaris traces (v9.187 / roadmap P1.6). Dashboards-as-code over the Tempo datasource. The correlation id is the join key: an X-Request-ID from a caller or a structured-log line finds its trace via span.polaris.request_id.
title: Polaris — Traces

options.content:
**Log line → trace:** every `structured_log` JSON line carries `trace_id`/`span_id` while its request's span was recording — paste the `trace_id` into Tempo's TraceQL search or Explore.

**X-Request-ID → trace:** the id echoed to a caller (and stamped on every log line as `request_id`) is on the request span as `polaris.request_id`. Type it into the *X-Request-ID* box above; the panel below finds the trace. TraceQL: `{span.polaris.request_id="<id>"}`.

**Trace → log lines:** `docker logs polaris-app | jq 'select(.trace_id=="<trace_id>")'`.

Ids are ephemeral by design (v9.122): minted per request, never derived from identity, never written to the database. Traces live only in your Tempo under its retention (7 days in the shipped config).

panels.title: Find by correlation id
panels.description: Fill the X-Request-ID variable above. Empty matches nothing (by design — this panel answers a quoted id, it is not a firehose).

panels.title: Slow requests (> 500ms)
panels.description: The P1.9 performance-baseline conversation starts here: which spans inside the request carry the time — the DB client span (statement template, never values) or the app between them?

panels.title: Errored requests
panels.description: Server spans marked ERROR (5xx or an unhandled exception; status carries the exception CLASS only — messages and stacks stay in the logs, joined by trace_id).
